summary: You can now add a transition from a right-click on a clip or the ruler, or by dragging a tile, and the timeline lights up every place a tile can land. A clip's first and last frames take a fade from or to black. A join with no spare frames says so and offers Dip to black.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Two or three recordings back to back on V1 (drop a recording onto the end of the first one).

try.do: With nothing picked, look at the Transitions section, then click the Cross dissolve tile.
Drag the Cross dissolve tile over the middle of a clip and read the timeline's bar.
Let go of it on a lit join.
Command Z, then right-click the middle clip and choose Add Transition > Cross dissolve.
Press Use Dip to black on the notice.
Right-click the first clip and choose Add Transition > Cross dissolve.
Right-click the ruler over a join and choose Add Transition > Wipe.

evaluate: With nothing picked, does the one line in the Transitions section tell you what the tiles are for?
When you click a tile with no join picked, do the lit marks on the timeline tell you where to take it?
Are the white marks (lands) and the dark red-ringed marks (no spare frames) easy to tell apart on every clip colour?
Is it right that Cross dissolve at a clip end with nothing next to it fades from or to black, the way Premiere does?
Is '1 cut skipped / No spare frames at 0:15' with a Use Dip to black button the answer you want when one end could not take it?
rough: The lit marks only show while a tile is over the timeline or for 2.5 seconds after a click. They do not light the moment the tile leaves the panel, because a drag gives no signal when it ends outside the timeline.
The section's hint, 'Drag a tile onto a cut on the timeline', is the first half of the mock's line in fewer words. The mock's whole line still sits behind the question mark.

The walks drive the drop through the timeline's own drop target, and a real pointer was proved to pick the tile up. The system's drag loop between the two cannot be driven by a walk, so a real hand-made drag from panel to timeline is still for you to try.

Push, Wipe, Blur through and Dip to white at a clip end with nothing next to it say 'needs a clip on both sides' rather than offering something. Only Cross dissolve and Dip to black become a fade there.
The mock's six tiles (Dip to color, Slide, Morph, Cut) are still not the app's six. That was already so before this task.
